stem: A lung transplant candidate on the waitlist has overdue organ-specific laboratory studies needed to maintain an active LAS. What is the coordinator's appropriate action?

options.text: Arrange required studies and educate the candidate that failure to complete testing may change waitlist priority
Remove the candidate permanently from the waitlist without discussion
Defer all waitlist testing until after transplantation
Assume overdue studies have no effect on allocation status

explanation.rationale_correct: Transplant coordinators arrange waitlist studies and educate candidates that failure to complete required organ-specific testing, such as LAS or MELD updates, may change priority on the waitlist.

rationale_incorrect.B: Overdue testing triggers coordination and education; permanent delisting without process is not the described standard response.
rationale_incorrect.C: Required waitlist studies must be completed while waiting to remain viable candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Failure to complete required testing may change candidate priority on the waitlist.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §b. Waitlist management → c.i.–iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Failure to complete required testing may result in a change in candidate's priority on the waitlist

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §b. Waitlist management → c.ii. and coordinator responsibilities c.iii.–iv.; PDF p. 102 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Third 020700 item; waitlist maintenance angle distinct from cctc-2008/2016; anchor verified on Cupples p. 102.

stem: When explaining the kidney transplant evaluation process to a candidate, how should the coordinator frame the purpose of evaluation?

options.text: Determine the optimal mode of ESKD care after multiple considerations, not merely a yes-or-no transplant decision
Provide a one-time pass/fail verdict with no role for shared decision-making
Guarantee immediate transplantation for every referred patient
Exclude patient advocacy because the team decides without candidate input

explanation.rationale_correct: Kidney transplant evaluation should determine the optimal mode of end-stage kidney disease care after multiple considerations, with patient advocacy as the guiding principle rather than a simple thumbs-up or thumbs-down.

rationale_incorrect.B: Evaluation is designed for individualized care planning, not a single opaque pass/fail without discussion.
rationale_incorrect.C: Referral and evaluation do not guarantee immediate transplantation for every patient.
rationale_incorrect.D: Patient advocacy remains the guiding principle throughout evaluation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 8, Evaluation of Adult Kidney Transplant Candidates → evaluation purpose paragraph
primary_anchor.quote_hint: determine the optimal mode of ESKD care after multiple considerations are taken into account

references.locator: Ch. 8 → Part I evaluation purpose (optimal ESKD care, patient advocacy); PDF p. 227 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fourth 020200 item; anchor verified on Danovitch p. 227.

stem: A heart-lung transplant candidate completes organ-specific tests and consultations. What is the next standard step before listing consideration?

options.text: Present the completed evaluation to the transplant selection committee
Enter the candidate directly into UNet without team review
Schedule transplantation before any committee review
Skip documentation because heart-lung candidates are automatically listed

explanation.rationale_correct: Heart-lung transplant evaluation combines individual organ tests, procedures, and consults that, when completed, are presented to the transplant selection committee for listing consideration.

rationale_incorrect.B: Listing follows selection committee review and appropriate UNOS data entry, not automatic listing without team presentation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Surgery is not scheduled before evaluation completion and listing consideration.
rationale_incorrect.D: Heart-lung candidates require formal evaluation presentation, not automatic listing.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: presented to the transplant selection committee for listing consideration

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 11 → heart-lung transplantation → C. Evaluation → 1. (selection committee presentation); PDF p. 626 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fourth 020600 item; second heart_lung organ tag; distinct from DonorNet/PHS angles; anchor verified on Cupples p. 626.

stem: A liver transplant candidate has a history of diabetes and former tobacco use. Which pretransplant cardiac testing is MOST appropriate per standard evaluation references?

options.text: Cardiac stress testing to evaluate myocardial perfusion
No cardiac testing because extracardiac transplant candidates never need cardiac evaluation
Immediate transplant without any cardiovascular assessment

explanation.rationale_correct: Patients with diabetes or smoking history require cardiac stress testing to evaluate myocardial perfusion as part of pretransplant consultation to identify perioperative cardiovascular risk.

rationale_incorrect.B: All transplant candidates receive cardiac evaluation; higher-risk histories warrant stress testing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Pretransplant evaluation identifies cardiovascular risks that may affect outcomes before proceeding.
rationale_incorrect.D: LAS applies to lung allocation, not liver candidate cardiac stress testing.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Consultations → J.1.c. cardiac stress testing
primary_anchor.quote_hint: diabetes, or smoking will require a cardiac stress test to evaluate myocardial perfusion

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → J. Consultations → 1. Cardiac evaluation → c. (stress testing for diabetes/smoking history); PDF p. 33 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
